ko_meaning: 기대한 것과 달라서 마음이 좋지 않다
ko_meaning_en: To feel bad because things did not turn out as you expected

example.en: I saw my exam results and was very disappointed.

form.q_en: Pick the particle that marks the person you are disappointed in.
form.why: You are disappointed 'in' a person: 사람 + 에게 실망하다. 에서 is for places, and 를/로 do not go with 실망하다.

ko_meaning: 전에 한 일이 잘못되었다고 생각하며 마음 아파하다
ko_meaning_en: To feel sorry, thinking that something you did before was wrong

example.ko: 그때 공부를 안 한 것을 후회해요.
example.roman: Geuttae gongbureul an han geoseul huhoehaeyo.
example.en: I regret not studying back then.

tokens.note: 안 makes the next verb negative
-ㄴ 것 turns the phrase into a noun

form.q_en: Pick the right modifier for something done in the past.
form.why: 그때 points to the past, so use the past modifier 한 before 것. 하는 is present, 할 is future, and 해서 cannot come before 것.

ko_meaning: 원하는 것이 이루어져서 마음에 들다
ko_meaning_en: To be pleased because what you wanted came true

example.en: I was very satisfied with the accommodation this time.

tokens.note: 에 marks what you are satisfied with

form.q_en: Pick the particle used with 만족하다.
form.why: 만족하다 takes 에 for the thing you are satisfied with. 에게서 is for people, and 으로 cannot follow a vowel.

ko_meaning: 걱정이 되어서 마음이 편하지 않고 몸이 굳다
ko_meaning_en: To feel uneasy and stiff because you are worried

example.en: I was so nervous when I had my job interview.

tokens.note: 면접을 보다 = to have an interview

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 때 'when'.
form.why: 때 'when' takes the -(으)ㄹ form, even for past events: 볼 때. 본, 보는 and 봐서 cannot come before 때.

en: to be moved; to be touched
ko_meaning: 어떤 것을 보거나 듣고 마음이 크게 움직이다
ko_meaning_en: To feel your heart deeply stirred by something you see or hear

example.en: I was so moved while watching that movie that I cried.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'while'.
form.why: -(으)면서 means 'while' doing two things at the same time. -(으)면 means 'if', and -(으)러 / -(으)려고 show purpose.

ko_meaning: 사람마다 다른 마음과 행동의 특징
ko_meaning_en: The way of thinking and acting that differs from person to person

example.en: My younger sibling has a very cheerful personality.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 성격 in 'A는 B가 + adjective'.
form.why: 성격 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이. 가 follows a vowel, and 을/를 mark objects.

en: to be lively; to be active
ko_meaning: 행동이 힘 있고 밝다
ko_meaning_en: Acting with lots of energy and cheerfulness

example.en: My older sister has a lively personality, so she has many friends.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that gives the reason.
form.why: -아서/어서 gives a reason: lively, so many friends. -지만 shows contrast, and -(으)러 / -(으)려고 show purpose.

ko_meaning: 작은 것까지 잘 살피고 실수가 없다
ko_meaning_en: Checking even small things carefully and making no mistakes

example.en: The department head checks documents thoroughly.

tokens.note: -게 turns an adjective into an adverb

form.q_en: Pick the form that describes HOW he checks.
form.why: -게 turns the adjective into an adverb that describes the verb. 꼼꼼한 must come before a noun.

ko_meaning: 움직이거나 일하기를 싫어하다
ko_meaning_en: Not liking to move or work

example.ko: 동생은 게을러서 방 청소를 안 해요.
example.roman: Dongsaeng-eun geeulleoseo bang cheongsoreul an haeyo.
example.en: My younger sibling is lazy, so they don't clean their room.

form.q_en: Pick the correct -어서 form of 게으르다.
form.why: 게으르다 is 르-irregular: 르 drops its vowel and an extra ㄹ is added, so 게으르 + 어서 → 게을러서.

ko_meaning: 게으르지 않고 늘 열심히 움직이다
ko_meaning_en: Always working hard and never being lazy

example.en: My grandmother is diligent, so she gets up at dawn every day.

form.q_en: Pick the correct connecting form.
form.why: -아서/어서 gives the reason. 부지런하다 is an adjective, so -는 is wrong, and -(으)러 shows purpose with movement verbs.

en: to be honest; to be frank
ko_meaning: 거짓 없이 생각을 그대로 말하다
ko_meaning_en: Saying what you think as it is, without lying

example.ko: 솔직하게 말하면 그 음식은 별로 맛이 없었어요.
example.roman: Soljikage malhamyeon geu eumsigeun byeollo masi eopseosseoyo.
example.en: To be honest, that food wasn't very tasty.

tokens.note: -게 turns an adjective into an adverb
별로 is used with a negative

form.q_en: Complete the set phrase 'to be honest'.
form.ko: 솔직하게 ___ 그 음식은 별로 맛이 없었어요.
form.why: 솔직하게 말하면 'if I speak honestly' is a fixed way to say 'to be honest'. -(으)러 and -(으)려고 show purpose, and 말한 must come before a noun.

en: to be sincere; to be hardworking
ko_meaning: 자기가 맡은 일을 늘 열심히 하다
ko_meaning_en: Always working hard on the tasks you are given

example.ko: 동료가 성실하기 때문에 같이 일하기 편해요.
example.roman: Dongnyoga seongsilhagi ttaemune gachi ilhagi pyeonhaeyo.
example.en: My colleague is hardworking, so it's easy to work together.

tokens.note: -기 turns the verb into a noun

form.q_en: Pick the ending that goes before 때문에.
form.ko: 동료가 성실하___ 때문에 같이 일하기 편해요.
form.why: After a verb or adjective, 때문에 needs -기: 성실하기 때문에 'because (he) is hardworking'.

ko_meaning: 자기를 자랑하지 않고 낮추다
ko_meaning_en: Not boasting and keeping yourself humble

example.en: That athlete is famous but very modest.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that shows contrast.
form.why: -지만 shows contrast: famous, but modest. 유명하서 is not a correct form, and fame is not a reason or condition for being modest.

ko_meaning: 자기 생각을 바꾸지 않고 끝까지 지키려는 마음
ko_meaning_en: A mind that refuses to change its own idea and holds on to it to the end

example.ko: 아이가 고집이 세서 말을 안 들어요.
example.roman: Aiga gojibi seseo mareul an deureoyo.
example.en: The child is so stubborn that he doesn't listen.

tokens.note: 말을 듣다 = to obey; ㄷ irregular: 듣다 → 들어요

form.q_en: Which adjective goes with 고집 for 'very stubborn'?
form.why: Koreans say 고집이 세다 'stubbornness is strong'. 높다, 길다 and 크다 are not used with 고집.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람을 대할 때 지켜야 하는 바른 말과 행동
ko_meaning_en: The proper words and behavior to keep when dealing with others

example.en: It is important to show good manners to elders.

tokens.note: 예의를 지키다 = to show good manners
-는 것 turns the phrase into a noun

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 예의.
form.why: 예의 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를. 을 follows a consonant, and 가/에 do not mark the object of 지키다.

ko_meaning: 사람이 만들지 않은 산, 바다, 나무 같은 것
ko_meaning_en: Things that people did not make, such as mountains, seas and trees

example.en: On weekends I want to rest in nature.

tokens.note: 속 = inside; 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where you rest.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action like 쉬다 happens. 을 marks an object, 이 a subject, and 의 needs a noun after it.

ko_meaning: 나무가 많이 자라는 넓은 곳
ko_meaning_en: A wide place where many trees grow

example.en: I can hear birds singing in the forest.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the sound happens.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where something happens. 을/를 mark objects (를 never follows a consonant), and after a consonant 'and' is 과, not 와.

ko_meaning: 땅 위에 물이 많이 모여 있는 넓은 곳
ko_meaning_en: A wide place on land where a lot of water has gathered

example.en: We talked while walking beside the lake.

tokens.note: 을 with 걷다 marks the route

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 걷다 + -(으)면서.
form.why: 걷다 is ㄷ-irregular: before a vowel ㄷ becomes ㄹ, so 걷 + 으면서 → 걸으면서. 걸면서 comes from a different verb (걸다 'to hang').

ko_meaning: 바다 가운데에 있는 땅
ko_meaning_en: Land in the middle of the sea

example.en: Jeju Island is the biggest island in Korea.

form.q_en: Pick the right form of 'is' after 섬.
form.why: 섬 ends in a consonant, so it takes 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 아주 크고 딱딱한 돌
ko_meaning_en: A very big, hard stone

example.en: I sat on a rock and looked at the sea.

tokens.note: N 위에 = on top of N
-아서 links actions where the first one continues

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'sat and (then, sitting) looked'.
form.why: -아서 links two actions where the first one continues: you sit, then look while sitting. -(으)러 / -(으)려고 show purpose, and -(으)면 means 'if'.

ko_meaning: 공기가 얼마나 덥거나 추운지를 나타내는 숫자
ko_meaning_en: The number showing how hot or cold the air is

example.en: They say the temperature will drop a lot tomorrow.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reported-speech form of the verb 떨어지다.
form.why: For verbs, reported speech uses -ㄴ다고/는다고 하다: 떨어진다고 해요. Plain -다고 is for adjectives (e.g. 춥다고).

ko_meaning: 여름에 오랫동안 비가 계속 내리는 때
ko_meaning_en: The time in summer when it rains for a long time

example.ko: 장마 때문에 빨래가 잘 안 말라요.
example.roman: Jangma ttaemune ppallaega jal an mallayo.
example.en: Because of the rainy season, the laundry doesn't dry well.

form.q_en: Pick the right way to say 'because of' after a noun.
form.why: After a noun, 때문에 comes directly: 장마 때문에 'because of the rainy season'. -기 때문에 is for verbs and adjectives.

ko_meaning: 비와 아주 센 바람이 함께 오는 큰 바람
ko_meaning_en: A huge storm that brings rain and very strong wind together

example.en: A typhoon came, so the plane couldn't take off.

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'couldn't'.
form.why: -지 못하다 means 'could not' because of an outside cause. The long negative uses 않다 (never 안 하다), and -지 말다 is only for commands.

ko_meaning: 갑자기 많이 오다가 금방 끝나는 비
ko_meaning_en: Rain that suddenly pours and soon ends

example.en: I was on my way home when a sudden shower came.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that sets the background.
form.why: -는데 gives the background situation (I was going home) for what happened next. -(으)면 means 'if', and -(으)려고 shows purpose.

ko_meaning: 작은 물방울이 공기 중에 떠 있어서 앞이 잘 안 보이는 것
ko_meaning_en: Tiny water drops floating in the air so that you cannot see ahead well

example.ko: 안개가 껴서 앞이 잘 안 보여요.
example.roman: Angaega kkyeoseo api jal an boyeoyo.
example.en: The fog has rolled in, so I can't see well ahead.

tokens.note: 안개가 끼다 = fog sets in; 끼 + 어서 → 껴서

form.q_en: Which verb goes with 안개?
form.why: Koreans say 안개가 끼다 for fog setting in. 불다 goes with wind, 뜨다 with the sun or moon, and 타다 means 'to ride' or 'to burn'.

ko_meaning: 사람이나 동물이 살아가는 주변의 자연과 상태
ko_meaning_en: The nature and conditions around where people and animals live

example.en: We all need to think about the environment.

form.q_en: Pick the form for 'must / need to'.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 means 'must / need to': 생각해야 해요. -(으)러, -(으)면 and -지 do not combine with 해요 like this.

ko_meaning: 필요 없어서 버리는 더러운 것
ko_meaning_en: Dirty or unneeded things that you throw away

example.en: You must not throw trash on the street.

form.q_en: Complete 'must not'.
form.why: -(으)면 안 되다 is the fixed pattern for 'must not'. 못, 말 and 없 do not fit before 돼요.

ko_meaning: 쓰고 난 물건을 다시 쓸 수 있게 만드는 것
ko_meaning_en: Making used things usable again

example.en: Paper and bottles can be recycled.

form.q_en: Complete 'can (be done)'.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 means 'can'. 때, 적 and 줄 belong to other patterns.

ko_meaning: 돈이나 물건을 꼭 필요한 만큼만 쓰다
ko_meaning_en: To use money or things only as much as you need

example.en: The habit of using water sparingly is important.

tokens.note: 아끼 + 어 → 아껴; 아껴 쓰다 = to use sparingly

form.q_en: Pick the correct form before 쓰다.
form.why: 아끼 + 어 combines into 아껴, and 아껴 쓰다 means 'to use sparingly'. 아낀 must come before a noun.

ko_meaning: 필요 없는 물건을 쓰레기통 같은 곳에 넣다
ko_meaning_en: To put things you don't need into a trash can or similar place

example.en: I decided to throw away the clothes I don't wear.

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'decided to'.
form.why: -기로 하다 means 'to decide to (do)'. -기에, -러 and -면서 cannot be followed by 했어요 like this.

ko_meaning: 숨을 쉴 때 들어오는, 눈에 보이지 않는 것
ko_meaning_en: The invisible thing that comes in when you breathe

example.en: Now that I'm in the mountains, the air is really clean.

tokens.note: -(으)니까 can show what you find after doing something

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 맑다.
form.why: The stem 맑 has the vowel ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 맑아요 (pronounced [말가요], but written 맑아요).

ko_meaning: 물, 공기, 땅 등이 더러워지는 것
ko_meaning_en: Water, air, land, etc. becoming dirty

example.en: The river got polluted because of the factory.

form.q_en: Pick the right verb form for 'the river got polluted'.
form.why: The river is what gets polluted, so use 오염되다. 오염시키다 needs someone polluting something (공장이 강을 오염시켰어요).

ko_meaning: 공기 속에 있는 아주 작은 먼지
ko_meaning_en: Very tiny dust in the air

example.en: The fine dust is bad today, so wear a mask.

tokens.note: -(으)니까 gives a reason before a request

form.q_en: Pick the reason ending that can come before a request.
form.why: Before a request like -(으)세요, use -(으)니까 for the reason. -아서/어서 cannot be followed by a request or command.

ko_meaning: 위험하거나 나쁜 것으로부터 잘 지키다
ko_meaning_en: To keep something safe from danger or harm

example.ko: 숲을 보호하는 것은 우리 모두의 일이에요.
example.roman: Supeul bohohaneun geoseun uri moduui irieyo.
example.en: Protecting the forests is a job for all of us.

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 것 to mean 'the act of protecting'.
form.ko: 숲을 보호하___ 것은 우리 모두의 일이에요.
form.why: To make 'the act of doing' with 것, use the present modifier -는: 보호하는 것.

ko_meaning: 한 번만 쓰고 버리는 물건
ko_meaning_en: Things you use only once and then throw away

example.en: These days cafes don't use disposable products.

form.q_en: Pick the word that completes the long negative.
form.why: The long negative is -지 않다: 쓰지 않아요. 안 해요, 없어요 and 아니에요 cannot follow -지.

ko_meaning: 땅에 뿌리를 내리고 자라는 꽃, 풀, 나무 같은 것
ko_meaning_en: Things such as flowers, grass and trees that grow with roots in the ground

example.ko: 식물은 햇빛이 없으면 잘 자라지 못해요.
example.roman: Singmureun haetbichi eopseumyeon jal jaraji motaeyo.
example.en: Plants can't grow well without sunlight.

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 못하다.
form.why: -지 못하다 'cannot' needs -지 on the verb: 자라지 못해요.

ko_meaning: 나무나 풀에 달린 얇고 보통 초록색인 것
ko_meaning_en: The thin, usually green parts growing on trees and plants

example.en: When autumn comes, the leaves turn red.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for what something turns into.
form.why: 변하다 uses (으)로 for the new state. 빨간색 ends in a consonant, so 으로; 로 follows a vowel or ㄹ.

ko_meaning: 줄기가 부드럽고 키가 작은 식물
ko_meaning_en: A short plant with soft stems

example.en: The cow is eating grass.

form.q_en: Pick the ending for an action in progress.
form.why: -고 있다 shows an action in progress: 먹고 있어요 'is eating'.

ko_meaning: 다리가 여섯 개이고 몸이 머리, 가슴, 배로 나뉜 작은 동물
ko_meaning_en: A small animal with six legs whose body is divided into head, chest and belly

example.en: My son is very interested in insects.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for what you are interested in.
form.why: 관심이 많다/있다 'to be interested' takes 에 for the thing you are interested in.

ko_meaning: 동물이나 식물을 돌보아 자라게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To look after animals or plants so that they grow

example.ko: 어렸을 때 강아지를 키운 적이 있어요.
example.roman: Eoryeosseul ttae gangajireul kiun jeogi isseoyo.
example.en: I raised a puppy when I was a child.

form.q_en: Pick the form for 'have done before'.
form.why: -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다 'have done before' uses the past modifier -(으)ㄴ: 키운 적이 있어요.

ko_meaning: 청소, 빨래, 요리처럼 집 안에서 하는 일
ko_meaning_en: Work done at home, like cleaning, laundry and cooking

example.en: On weekends I do housework together with my husband.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 집안일.
form.why: 집안일 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so the object particle is 을. 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 밥을 먹은 뒤에 그릇을 씻는 일
ko_meaning_en: Washing the bowls and dishes after a meal

example.en: When Mom cooks, I do the dishes.

tokens.note: 설거지를 하다 = to do the dishes

form.q_en: Pick the right ending for what YOU do.
form.why: Never use the honorific -(으)시- for yourself: 제가 ... 해요. Only 엄마 gets -시- (요리하시면).

ko_meaning: 어지러운 것을 제자리에 깨끗하게 놓다
ko_meaning_en: To put messy things neatly back in their places

example.en: I tried organizing my wardrobe over the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the form for 'tried doing'.
form.why: -아/어 보다 'try doing' needs the -아/어 form: 정리해 봤어요.

ko_meaning: 더러운 것을 천이나 휴지로 문질러 깨끗하게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To rub dirt off with a cloth or tissue to make something clean

example.en: Brush your teeth after eating.

tokens.note: 이를 닦다 = to brush teeth; -(으)세요 = please

form.q_en: Which verb goes with 이 'teeth'?
form.why: Koreans say 이를 닦다 'to brush teeth'. 감다 is for hair, 빨다 for laundry, and 청소하다 for rooms.

ko_meaning: 빗자루로 바닥의 먼지나 쓰레기를 모아 치우다
ko_meaning_en: To gather and clear dust or trash on the floor with a broom

example.en: I sweep in front of the store every morning.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 쓸다.
form.why: 쓸다 is regular before -어요: 쓸 + 어요 → 쓸어요. Don't mix it up with 쓰다 → 써요.

ko_meaning: 뜨거운 다리미로 옷을 눌러서 반듯하게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To press clothes flat with a hot iron

example.en: I ironed my shirt the day before the interview.

form.q_en: Pick the past form of 다리다 'to iron'.
form.why: 다리다 → 다렸어요. 달렸어요 is from 달리다 'to run', and 달랐어요 from 다르다 'to be different'.

ko_meaning: 빨래를 말리려고 줄이나 대에 펴서 걸다
ko_meaning_en: To spread wet laundry on a line or rack to dry

example.en: The weather was nice, so I hung the laundry outside.

form.q_en: Pick the verb for hanging laundry.
form.why: 널다 'to hang out laundry' → 널었어요. 넣다 means 'to put in', and 놀다 'to play'.

ko_meaning: 옷이나 이불을 접어서 작게 만들다
ko_meaning_en: To fold clothes or bedding into a small, neat shape

example.en: When I get up in the morning, I fold my bedding.

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'fold, and then'.
form.why: -고 links two actions in order: fold the bedding, then clean the room. -러 and -려면 show purpose, and 개는 needs a noun after it.

ko_meaning: 쓰레기를 버리는 통
ko_meaning_en: A container you throw trash into

example.ko: 다 먹은 컵은 저 쓰레기통에 버리세요.
example.roman: Da meogeun keobeun jeo sseuregitong-e beoriseyo.
example.en: Throw the cups you've finished into that trash can.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you throw something.
form.ko: 다 먹은 컵은 저 쓰레기통___ 버리세요.
form.why: 에 marks where something goes: 쓰레기통에 버리다. 을 marks an object, 이 a subject, and 와 means 'and'.

ko_meaning: 쓰레기를 종류에 따라 나누어서 버리는 것
ko_meaning_en: Sorting trash by type before throwing it out

example.en: Our apartment complex sorts recycling on Wednesdays.

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 때 'when'.
form.why: 때 'when' takes the -(으)ㄹ form: 할 때 'when (you) do'.

ko_meaning: 사는 곳을 다른 곳으로 옮기다
ko_meaning_en: To change the place where you live

example.ko: 다음 달에 회사 근처로 이사하게 됐어요.
example.roman: Daeum dare hoesa geuncheoro isahage dwaesseoyo.
example.en: It turns out I'm moving near my office next month.

tokens.note: -게 되다 = end up doing / it turns out

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'it turned out that ...'.
form.ko: 다음 달에 회사 근처로 이사하___ 됐어요.
form.why: -게 되다 means 'to end up doing / it turns out that'. -기, -고 and -러 do not combine with 되다 this way.

ko_meaning: 한 건물 안에 여러 집이 층층이 있는 높은 집
ko_meaning_en: A tall building with many homes stacked floor by floor

example.en: This apartment is close to the subway station, so it's convenient.

form.q_en: Pick the correct -어서 form of 가깝다.
form.why: 가깝다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 가깝 + 어서 → 가까워서. 가까와서 is an old spelling.

ko_meaning: 방 하나에 부엌과 화장실이 같이 있는 작은 집
ko_meaning_en: A small home with one room plus a kitchen and bathroom

example.en: I live alone, so I found a small studio apartment.

tokens.note: 구하다 = to look for and get

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 살다.
form.why: 살다 + 아서 → 살아서. ㄹ-stem verbs never take 으: the other endings would be 살면서 and 사니까.

ko_meaning: 집이나 방을 빌려 쓰고 달마다 내는 돈
ko_meaning_en: Money you pay every month to rent a house or room

example.en: Monthly rent in Seoul is too expensive.

form.q_en: Pick the right way to give the reason.
form.why: -기 때문에 gives a reason. 덕분에 'thanks to' is used for good results, not for a problem like high rent.

ko_meaning: 큰돈을 집주인에게 맡기고 집을 빌려 사는 것, 나갈 때 그 돈을 다시 받는다
ko_meaning_en: Renting a home by leaving a large sum with the owner, which you get back when you move out

example.en: I heard jeonse is better than monthly rent.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reported-speech form of the adjective 좋다.
form.why: For adjectives, reported speech uses -다고: 좋다고 들었어요. -ㄴ다고/는다고 is only for verbs.

ko_meaning: 집을 가지고 있으면서 다른 사람에게 빌려주는 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person who owns a house and rents it out to others

example.en: I contacted the landlord, but there's no reply yet.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that shows contrast here.
form.why: -는데 here shows contrast with what you expected: I contacted him, but there's no reply yet.

ko_meaning: 서로 지켜야 할 것을 약속하고 글로 써서 정하는 것
ko_meaning_en: Agreeing in writing on what both sides must keep

example.en: My contract period is over, so I have to move.

form.q_en: Pick the reason ending.
form.why: -아서/어서 gives the reason: the contract ended, so I must move. -(으)러 and -(으)려고 show purpose, and 끝난 needs a noun after it.

ko_meaning: 아파트 같은 건물에서 청소, 전기, 물 등에 매달 내는 돈
ko_meaning_en: Money paid every month in a building like an apartment for cleaning, electricity, water, etc.

example.ko: 겨울에는 난방 때문에 관리비가 많이 나와요.
example.roman: Gyeoureneun nanbang ttaemune gwallibiga mani nawayo.
example.en: In winter the maintenance fee is high because of heating.

form.q_en: Which verb is used for a bill amount?
form.why: For bills, Koreans say 관리비/요금이 나오다 'the bill comes out (to an amount)'. 걷다, 열다 and 입다 make no sense with a fee.

ko_meaning: 기계나 물건이 망가져서 제대로 움직이지 않는 것
ko_meaning_en: A machine or object being broken so that it doesn't work properly

example.ko: 세탁기가 고장 나서 빨래를 못 했어요.
example.roman: Setakgiga gojang naseo ppallaereul mot haesseoyo.
example.en: The washing machine broke down, so I couldn't do the laundry.

form.q_en: Which verb goes with 고장?
form.why: Koreans say 고장(이) 나다 'to break down'. 고장하다 and 고장받다 are not used.

ko_meaning: 고장 나거나 망가진 것을 고치다
ko_meaning_en: To fix something that is broken

example.en: The landlord fixed the boiler for me.

form.q_en: Pick the form for 'do something for someone'.
form.why: -아/어 주다 'do something for someone' needs the -아/어 form: 수리해 줬어요.

ko_meaning: 동네 사람들이 서류를 받거나 여러 일을 보러 가는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A local office where residents get documents and take care of various matters

example.ko: 주민센터에서 한국어 수업을 무료로 들을 수 있어요.
example.roman: Juminsenteoeseo hangugeo sueobeul muryoro deureul su isseoyo.
example.en: You can take Korean classes for free at the community service center.

tokens.note: 수업을 듣다 = to take a class

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 듣다 before 수 있다.
form.ko: 주민센터에서 한국어 수업을 무료로 ___ 수 있어요.
form.why: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: 듣 + 을 → 들을. -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 needs the -(으)ㄹ form.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 해 달라고 서류를 내거나 요청하다
ko_meaning_en: To ask for something officially, for example by handing in a form

example.en: Can I apply for a visa online?

form.q_en: Pick the form used before 수 있다.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 'can' always uses the -(으)ㄹ form: 신청할 수 있어요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일에 필요한 내용을 적은 종이
ko_meaning_en: Papers with the information needed for some task

example.en: I prepared all the necessary documents.

form.q_en: Pick the right modifier form of the adjective 필요하다.
form.why: 필요하다 is an adjective, so before a noun it takes -(으)ㄴ: 필요한 서류. -는 is for verbs.

ko_meaning: 한국에 오래 사는 외국인에게 나라에서 만들어 주는 카드
ko_meaning_en: A card the government issues to foreigners who live in Korea long-term

example.ko: 은행에서 계좌를 만들 때 외국인등록증이 필요해요.
example.roman: Eunhaeng-eseo gyejwareul mandeul ttae oegugindeungnokjeung-i piryohaeyo.
example.en: When you open a bank account, you need your alien registration card.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 만들다 before 때.
form.why: 만들다 ends in ㄹ, so its -(으)ㄹ form is simply 만들: 만들 때.

ko_meaning: 기관에서 서류나 카드 등을 만들어 내주는 것
ko_meaning_en: An office making and handing out documents, cards and so on

example.ko: 여권 발급은 보통 일주일 정도 걸려요.
example.roman: Yeogwon balgeubeun botong iljuil jeongdo geollyeoyo.
example.en: Issuing a passport usually takes about a week.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for what takes time.
form.ko: 여권 발급___ 보통 일주일 정도 걸려요.
form.why: The thing that takes time is the topic here: 발급은 ... 걸려요. 걸리다 takes no object (을), and 과 means 'and'.

ko_meaning: 편지나 물건을 우체국을 통해 보내는 것
ko_meaning_en: Sending letters or goods through the post office

example.en: We will send the results by mail.

form.q_en: Pick the particle that shows the means.
form.why: (으)로 marks the means. 우편 ends in a consonant (ㄴ), so 으로.

ko_meaning: 우체국을 통해 보내는, 종이 등으로 싼 물건
ko_meaning_en: A wrapped package sent through the post office

example.en: My mom back in my hometown sent me a parcel.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 소포.
form.why: 소포 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를. 을 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 물건을 집이나 원하는 곳까지 배달해 주는 일
ko_meaning_en: A service that delivers goods to your home or wherever you want

example.en: The thing I bought online came by delivery.

form.q_en: Pick the modifier for something already bought.
form.why: The buying happened before, so use the past modifier -(으)ㄴ: 산 물건 'the thing I bought'.

ko_meaning: 물건이나 음식을 원하는 곳까지 가져다주는 것
ko_meaning_en: Bringing goods or food to where someone wants

example.en: This restaurant doesn't do delivery.

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 배달.
form.why: 배달 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이. 가 follows a vowel, and 되다 takes no object.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 경찰이나 기관에 알리다
ko_meaning_en: To tell the police or an official office about something

example.en: I saw an accident on the street and reported it right away.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for whom you report to.
form.why: You report 'to' the police: 경찰에 신고하다. 을 and 이 do not show where a report goes, and after a consonant 'and' is 과.

ko_meaning: 은행에 돈을 넣고 빼려고 만든 자기 이름의 기록
ko_meaning_en: A record in your name at a bank for putting in and taking out money

example.ko: 월급을 받을 계좌 번호를 알려 주세요.
example.roman: Wolgeubeul badeul gyejwa beonhoreul allyeo juseyo.
example.en: Please tell me the account number where you'll receive your salary.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 알리다 before 주세요.
form.why: 알리 + 어 combines into 알려, and 알려 주세요 means 'please let me know'.

ko_meaning: 은행에 넣고 뺀 돈을 적어 주는 작은 책
ko_meaning_en: A small book that records the money you put in and take out of the bank

example.en: I made a new bankbook at the bank.

form.q_en: Pick the correct purpose form of 만들다.
form.why: With ㄹ-stem verbs, -(으)러 is just -러: 만들 + 러 → 만들러 'in order to make'.

ko_meaning: 은행 등을 통해 다른 사람에게 돈을 보내다
ko_meaning_en: To send money to someone through a bank or similar

example.en: I send money to my parents every month.

form.q_en: Pick the polite particle for 'to (my parents)'.
form.why: 께 is the honorific form of 에게 'to (someone)', used for people you respect.

ko_meaning: 돈을 맡기거나 빌린 대가로 더 받거나 내는 돈
ko_meaning_en: Extra money you get for saving or pay for borrowing

example.en: Bank interest is too low these days.

form.q_en: Which adjective goes with 이자?
form.why: Interest is 높다 'high' or 낮다 'low'. 짧다, 가볍다 and 좁다 describe length, weight and width.

ko_meaning: 돈을 쓰지 않고 은행 등에 모아 두다
ko_meaning_en: To keep money in a bank instead of spending it

example.ko: 여행을 가려고 매달 조금씩 저금하고 있어요.
example.roman: Yeohaeng-eul garyeogo maedal jogeumssik jeogeumhago isseoyo.
example.en: I'm saving a little every month to go on a trip.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that shows purpose with any verb.
form.why: -(으)려고 shows purpose with any verb. -(으)러 is used only before movement verbs like 가다/오다.

ko_meaning: 직접 해 보거나 겪어 본 일
ko_meaning_en: Something you have done or gone through yourself

example.ko: 외국에서 혼자 살아 본 경험이 있어요?
example.roman: Oegugeseo honja sara bon gyeongheomi isseoyo?
example.en: Have you ever lived alone abroad?

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 보다.
form.why: -아/어 보다 needs the -아/어 form: 살아 본 경험 'the experience of having lived'.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 하기에 알맞은 때
ko_meaning_en: The right time to do something

example.ko: 이번 기회에 한국 문화를 배워 보세요.
example.roman: Ibeon gihoee hanguk munhwareul baewo boseyo.
example.en: Take this opportunity to learn about Korean culture.

form.q_en: Pick the particle in the set phrase 'taking this chance'.
form.ko: 이번 기회___ 한국 문화를 배워 보세요.
form.why: 이번 기회에 'on this occasion / taking this chance' is a set expression with 에.

ko_meaning: 이루고 싶어서 정해 놓은 일
ko_meaning_en: Something you set because you want to achieve it

example.ko: 올해 제 목표는 토픽 시험에 합격하는 것이에요.
example.roman: Olhae je mokpyoneun topik siheome hapgyeokaneun geosieyo.
example.en: My goal this year is to pass the TOPIK exam.

form.q_en: Pick the correct ending after 합격하는.
form.ko: 올해 제 목표는 토픽 시험에 합격하는 ___.
form.why: 것 ends in a consonant, so it takes 이에요: 것이에요 (in speech often 거예요).

ko_meaning: 앞으로 할 일을 미리 생각해서 정한 것
ko_meaning_en: What you have thought out and decided to do in advance

example.en: What plans do you have for the vacation?

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 계획 with 있다.
form.why: 계획 ends in a consonant, so it takes 이. 있다 takes a subject, not an object (을).

ko_meaning: 잘 때 보는 것, 또는 앞으로 꼭 이루고 싶은 일
ko_meaning_en: What you see while sleeping, or something you really want to achieve

example.en: I had a scary dream yesterday.

tokens.note: 꿈을 꾸다 = to have a dream

form.q_en: Which verb goes with 꿈?
form.why: Koreans say 꿈을 꾸다 'to have a dream': 꾸 + 었어요 → 꿨어요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일이 왜 그렇게 되었는지에 대한 까닭
ko_meaning_en: Why something happened or is the way it is

example.en: What is the reason you quit the company?

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 이유.
form.why: 이유 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가. 이 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 하는 길이나 수단
ko_meaning_en: The way or means of doing something

example.en: Is there an easy way to memorize words?

tokens.note: -게 turns an adjective into an adverb

form.q_en: Pick the adverb form 'easily'.
form.why: -게 turns 쉽다 into the adverb 쉽게 'easily', which describes 외우다. 쉬운 must come before a noun.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일이 끝난 뒤에 생긴 일이나 상태
ko_meaning_en: What comes about after something is finished

example.ko: 검사 결과는 다음 주에 나온다고 했어요.
example.roman: Geomsa gyeolgwaneun daeum jue naondago haesseoyo.
example.en: They said the test results will come out next week.

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle for 결과.
form.ko: 검사 결과___ 다음 주에 나온다고 했어요.
form.why: 결과 ends in a vowel, so the topic particle is 는. 은 follows a consonant, and the result is what comes out, so not 을.

ko_meaning: 풀어야 하는 어려운 일, 또는 시험에서 답을 내야 하는 물음
ko_meaning_en: A difficult matter to solve, or a question you must answer on a test

example.en: The exam questions were harder than I thought.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 어렵다.
form.why: 어렵다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 어렵 + 었어요 → 어려웠어요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일이 일어나고 있는 그때의 모습
ko_meaning_en: The state of things at the time something is happening

example.en: What should I do in a situation like this?

form.q_en: Pick the form for 'should'.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 means 'should / have to': 어떻게 해야 해요? 'What should I do?'

ko_meaning: 어떤 일에 대해 알려 주는 내용이나 자료
ko_meaning_en: Content or data that tells you about something

example.ko: 여행 정보는 인터넷에서 쉽게 찾을 수 있어요.
example.roman: Yeohaeng jeongboneun inteoneseseo swipge chajeul su isseoyo.
example.en: You can easily find travel information on the internet.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you search.
form.ko: 여행 정보는 인터넷___ 쉽게 찾을 수 있어요.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (찾다) happens. 에게 is for people.

ko_meaning: 말이나 글, 영화 등에 들어 있는 것
ko_meaning_en: What is contained in speech, writing, a movie, etc.

example.ko: 이 책은 내용이 어려워서 이해하기 힘들어요.
example.roman: I chaegeun naeyong-i eoryeowoseo ihaehagi himdeureoyo.
example.en: This book's content is difficult, so it's hard to understand.

tokens.note: -기 turns the verb into a noun

form.q_en: Pick the reason ending.
form.why: -아서/어서 gives the reason: difficult content, so hard to understand. -지만 shows contrast, and -(으)러 is for purpose.

ko_meaning: 말이나 글, 행동이 나타내는 뜻
ko_meaning_en: What a word, a text or an action expresses

example.en: I don't know the meaning of this word.

form.q_en: Pick the particle that links 'word' and 'meaning'.
form.why: 의 shows that one noun belongs to another: 단어의 의미 'the meaning of the word'.

ko_meaning: 서로 같지 않고 다른 정도
ko_meaning_en: How much two things are not the same

example.ko: 한국과 제 고향은 문화 차이가 커요.
example.roman: Hangukgwa je gohyang-eun munhwa chaiga keoyo.
example.en: There's a big cultural difference between Korea and my hometown.

form.q_en: Which adjective goes with 차이 for 'a big difference'?
form.why: Koreans say 차이가 크다 for a big difference. 길다, 무겁다 and 높다 do not go with 차이.

ko_meaning: 같은 특징을 가진 것끼리 나눈 무리
ko_meaning_en: A group of things sorted together because they share features

example.ko: 이 가게에는 여러 종류의 빵이 있어요.
example.roman: I gageeneun yeoreo jongnyuui ppang-i isseoyo.
example.en: This store has many kinds of bread.

form.q_en: Pick the word that goes right before 종류.
form.why: 여러 'several, many' comes directly before a noun: 여러 종류. 여럿 is a noun meaning 'many people/things'.

ko_meaning: 좋은 점이나 잘하는 점
ko_meaning_en: A good point or something one is good at

example.en: My strength is my meticulous personality.

form.q_en: Pick the humble word for 'my'.
form.why: 제 is the humble 'my' (저 + 의). 저, 제가 and 저는 cannot show possession.

ko_meaning: 모자라거나 좋지 않은 점
ko_meaning_en: A lacking or bad point

example.ko: 이 방은 좋은데 단점이 하나 있어요.
example.roman: I bang-eun joeunde danjeomi hana isseoyo.
example.en: This room is nice, but it has one drawback.

form.q_en: Pick the correct -는데 form of the adjective 좋다.
form.why: For adjectives, -는데 becomes -(으)ㄴ데: 좋은데 'it's nice, but'. 좋는데 is wrong.

ko_meaning: 다른 것과 비교해서 눈에 띄게 다른 점
ko_meaning_en: A point that clearly stands out compared with other things

example.ko: 이 지역 음식의 특징은 맵고 짠 거예요.
example.roman: I jiyeok eumsigui teukjingeun maepgo jjan geoyeyo.
example.en: The characteristic of this region's food is that it's spicy and salty.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that lists two qualities.
form.ko: 이 지역 음식의 특징은 ___ 짠 거예요.
form.why: -고 lists two qualities: 맵고 짜다 'spicy and salty'. -아서 gives a reason, and -지만 shows contrast.

ko_meaning: 사람이나 물건의 겉으로 보이는 모양이나 상태
ko_meaning_en: How a person or thing looks from the outside

example.ko: 아이가 열심히 공부하는 모습을 보니까 기분이 좋아요.
example.roman: Aiga yeolsimhi gongbuhaneun moseubeul bonikka gibuni joayo.
example.en: Seeing my child study hard makes me happy.

tokens.note: -(으)니까 gives the reason for a feeling

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'seeing ..., (I feel)'.
form.ko: 아이가 열심히 공부하는 모습을 ___ 기분이 좋아요.
form.why: -(으)니까 gives the reason for the feeling: seeing it makes me happy. -(으)러 and -(으)려고 show purpose.

ko_meaning: 사람이 매일 살아가면서 하는 여러 가지 일
ko_meaning_en: The various things a person does while living day to day

example.en: While living in Korea, I had many experiences.

tokens.note: 경험을 하다 = to have an experience

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'while'.
form.why: -(으)면서 'while' links two things happening over the same time. -(으)면 means 'if', and -(으)러 / -(으)려고 show purpose.

ko_meaning: 여러 가지 중에서 어떻게 할지 마음을 정하다
ko_meaning_en: To make up your mind about what to do among several options

example.en: After a lot of thought, I decided to quit the company.

tokens.note: 고민 끝에 = after a lot of thought

form.q_en: Pick the ending used before 결정하다 'decide to'.
form.why: -기로 결정하다 (or -기로 하다) means 'to decide to do'.

ko_meaning: 여러 가지 가운데서 필요하거나 마음에 드는 것을 고르다
ko_meaning_en: To pick what you need or like out of several things

example.en: Choose one of the two.

form.q_en: Pick the form of 'two' used before a counter.
form.why: Before a counter, 둘 becomes 두: 두 가지 'two kinds'.

ko_meaning: 맞는지 틀린지 다시 살펴보다
ko_meaning_en: To look again to make sure something is right

example.ko: 비행기 시간을 다시 한번 확인해 보세요.
example.roman: Bihaenggi siganeul dasi hanbeon hwaginhae boseyo.
example.en: Check your flight time once more.

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 보세요.
form.why: -아/어 보다 needs the -아/어 form: 확인하다 → 확인해 보세요.

ko_meaning: 둘 이상을 같이 놓고 같은 점과 다른 점을 살펴보다
ko_meaning_en: To look at two or more things side by side to find what is the same and what is different

example.en: Don't compare yourself with other people.

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'please don't'.
form.why: -지 마세요 is the polite way to say 'please don't'. 안 하세요, 없어요 and 아니에요 cannot follow -지.

ko_meaning: 모르는 사람끼리 서로 알게 해 주거나 어떤 것을 알려 주다
ko_meaning_en: To help people get to know each other, or to tell others about something

example.ko: 친구가 좋은 사람을 소개해 준다고 했어요.
example.roman: Chinguga joeun sarameul sogaehae jundago haesseoyo.
example.en: My friend said she would introduce me to a nice person.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reported-speech form of the verb 주다.
form.why: 주다 is a verb, so reported speech uses -ㄴ다고: 준다고 했어요. Plain -다고 is for adjectives.
